description:
FILED s425 (Fable) from the s423/#418 review probes, on main f02fe2a (B merged).  perl 5.40.3 vs PCL, `use utf8; our @ï¼¸=(1,2,3); our %ï¼¨=(k=>8); my $ï½=1; my $ï½='k';`:

    "$ï¼¸[$ï½]"            perl 2      PCL 1        <- SILENT WRONG (index read as undef -> 0)
    "$ï¼¨{$ï½}"            perl 8      PCL ""       <- SILENT WRONG
    "$ï¼¸[$ï½+1]"          perl 3      PCL dies: The function main::|pl-ï½| is undefined
    "@{[ $ï¼¸[0] + $ï¼¶ ]}"   perl 1      PCL dies: The function main::|pl-ï¼¸| is undefined
    "@{[ $ï¼¶ x 2 ]}", "${\ $ï¼¶}", "$ï¼¸[1]", "$ï¼¨{a}"   all CORRECT (no non-ASCII name inside a re-parsed fragment)

CAUSE: PPI splits `$ï½` into Cast + Word (ppi-upstream-bugs.md Â§23); PCL repairs that in Pl::Parser::_merge_unicode_symbols, called from the DOCUMENT-level _ppi_parse (Pl/Parser.pm ~561).  Every FRAGMENT re-parse builds its own PPI::Document and never runs the repair: Pl/PExpr/StringInterpolation.pm _interp_reparse (:311) and _parse_postfix_deref (:573), Pl/ExprToCL.pm :794 (_compile_ref_text_form, the regex consumer) and :3932, Pl/Parser.pm :693 :815 :851 :959 :9541 :9872, Pl/Parser2.pm :4212 (the mini-parse).  So `$ï½` inside "$ï¼¸[...]" arrives as `$` + bareword `ï½` = a symref to the undef ${"ï½"} -> 0, or a CALL to sub ï½ when an operator follows.  Pre-existing (the old StringInterpolation re-parsed the same fragments; #410 shipped s420 at document level only).

FIX SHAPE (rule 11): ONE fragment-document helper in Pl::Parser (new doc + _merge_unicode_symbols + whatever other in-place token repairs _ppi_parse applies to a document that a fragment can contain â check _reclassify_bare_vwords) and route EVERY site above through it; the caller keeps anchoring (#414).  The s409 ruling "a fragment mini-parse is the established pattern" stands â the pattern just needs the repairs.  NOTE: F/s427 (#422.2) is editing _reclass_subscripts_after in the same family; land this AFTER F merges, and re-run F's `$ï¼¸ {a}` probe through a fragment too.  Acceptance: the four rows above vs perl; guard rows in Pl/t/utf8-source-01.t; emission A/B over uni/+mro/ (the only population that can move) with every mover explained; ASCII byte-identical everywhere (the repair is a no-op on ASCII).


=== s438f (Opus 5, 2026-08-23) DONE, in the shape this task specified: ONE
fragment-document helper, `Pl::Parser::fragment_doc`, and every fragment
re-parse routed through it.

The helper builds the document and runs the three passes `_ppi_parse` applies
AFTER any serialize+reparse -- `_reclassify_bare_vwords`,
`_merge_unicode_symbols`, `_merge_punct_array_symbols`.  Those three are
exactly the ones that swap token CLASSES in place and leave the text untouched,
which is what makes them safe on a fragment; the passes that rewrite STRUCTURE
(signature desugaring, prototype attributes, `__SUB__`) must not run on a
fragment and do not.

NINE SITES routed: Pl/Parser.pm's `_replace_element` and the three
prototype/prologue splices, Pl/ExprToCL.pm x2, Pl/Parser2.pm's
`_rename_lexsub_in_code` mini-parse, and Pl/PExpr/StringInterpolation.pm's
`_interp_reparse` + `_parse_postfix_deref`.  NOT routed, deliberately and with
the reason in the helper's comment: `_normalize_signature_text`, which
re-serialises token TEXT -- the passes preserve text exactly, so it would buy
nothing and cost a walk on a guarded path.

A GATE CATCH WORTH RECORDING: the first version called
`Pl::Parser::fragment_doc` fully-qualified from the three other files, and
`Pl/t/string-interp-01.t` + `Pl/t/regexp-subst-01.t` died at
"Undefined subroutine" -- they load Pl::PExpr::StringInterpolation WITHOUT
Pl::Parser.  Under pl2cl the call always works (Parser is loaded first), so
corpus-diff, the four-population A/B and the full sweep were all clean while
the gate lost 97 rows.  A compile-time `use` would be circular (Parser ->
PExpr -> StringInterpolation -> Parser), so each cross-file site does a runtime
`require Pl::Parser` -- a %INC lookup once loaded.

MEASURED: the task's four reported rows plus its four controls all match perl
now (`"$ï¼¸[$ï½]"` 2, `"$ï¼¨{$ï½}"` 8, `"$ï¼¸[$ï½+1]"` 3, `"@{[ $ï¼¸[0] + $ï¼¶ ]}"` 2,
and `"@{[ $ï¼¶ x 2 ]}"` / `"${\ $ï¼¶}"` / `"$ï¼¸[1]"` / `"$ï¼¨{a}"` unchanged).
corpus-diff IDENTICAL over the 111; emission-ab over lib/**.pm +
cpan-tests/** + perl's own t/ (which includes uni/ and mro/, the population the
task expected to move) = 951 files SAME / 0 DIFF / 0 RCDIFF -- so the shape
occurs in no corpus and the guard rows are the bar (s371); gate 166/5771, only
the 13 pclxs xs rows; full sweep TOTAL 18312 (+0), GATE clean.  Guard: three
rows in Pl/t/utf8-source-01.t (25 -> 28), the third an ASCII inverse asserting
the identical shapes are untouched; inverse-guarded on a 94e89e3 worktree
(rows 26-27 fail there, 28 passes).
